step_by_step_reasoning: The whiteboard shows internal NHS Digital users on the left connecting to a public gateway EC2 (Guacamole) which authenticates against Directory Service (AD). On the secure sandbox side, a second EC2 converts existing datasets to Parquet and stores them in S3, encrypted with KMS keys. EMR reads the data from S3 to run analytics jobs. RDS is drawn but has no ledger connection and no flow explicitly described in the audio, so it is kept as a node with no edges. The ledger has 10 visual_connections entries; I emit 10 edges, one per entry with the same source and target, keeping both directions where listed. Flows: 0 = user login/authentication, 1 = data conversion and encrypted storage in S3, 2 = EMR analytics on S3 data.

graph.name: NHS Digital - Data Access Environment
graph.notes: Secure data access environment for NHS Digital internal teams. Users log into a public gateway (Guacamole) and work in a sandbox where data can be analysed but not extracted. Datasets are converted to Parquet, stored encrypted in S3 with KMS, and analysed with EMR. Access is controlled per user role via Apache Ranger.

nodes.name: NHS Digital internal users
nodes.notes: Internal teams within NHS Digital who log in to the data access environment.

nodes.name: EC2 - Public gateway / Auth service (Guacamole)
nodes.notes: Public gateway where users log into Guacamole; from there they enter a sandbox where they can view and analyse data but cannot get data out of the system.

nodes.name: EC2 - Data processing and conversion to Parquet
nodes.notes: Moves existing datasets and converts them to Parquet format before storing in S3.

nodes.name: RDS
nodes.notes: Drawn on the secure side of the whiteboard; its role is not described in the audio.

nodes.name: EMR
nodes.notes: Runs the analytics jobs and provides a consistent compute layer; reads data from S3. Jobs that took hours now take minutes or seconds. Apache Ranger enforces role-based data access; tooling such as RStudio, JupyterHub and Hue is offered.

nodes.name: Directory Service (AD)
nodes.notes: Authenticates users; the user's role is also used by the data processing tools to grant access to the right data.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Stores the converted Parquet files, always encrypted at rest and in transit.

nodes.name: KMS
nodes.notes: Provides the keys used to encrypt the data.

edges.notes: Users log into Guacamole on the public gateway.
Gateway authenticates the user against Directory Service.
Directory Service returns the user's identity and role.
User is given a sandbox session; data cannot be taken out of the system.
Existing datasets converted to Parquet are written to S3.
S3 requests a key from KMS to encrypt the data.
KMS provides the encryption key; data is always encrypted.
EMR reads the Parquet data from S3 to run analytics jobs.
